one_month_reasoning: Q3 earnings fall outside the window: CoreWeave reported Q2 on Aug 11 and Q3 is expected roughly Nov 5-16, with no date announced yet. Events inside the window: (1) the 35M-share Equity Distribution Agreement (ATM plus collared forwards, 8-K 9/17) can start about 30 days after the 9/17 convert purchase agreement, so from roughly Oct 17. That is up to ~6% potential supply, a mild overhang. (2) Ongoing 10b5-1 insider selling: seven Form 144s were filed 9/29-9/30 and the CEO sold 200k shares at $86.82 on 9/22. A mild negative. (3) Hyperscaler and Meta Q3 earnings in late October, where AI capex commentary moves neocloud stocks in either direction. (4) Convert hedge flows after the $4.2B 2033 notes (conversion price $97.85), which tend to damp upside near $98. No company-specific binary event, so I keep a near-symmetric lognormal on log price with a median of ~$87.6 (a slight tilt below $88.57 for the ATM and insider supply) and monthly sigma ~25%, close to the 93%/3.5 rule of thumb. Round 2: the supervisor confirmed the same event set (no Q3 date announced; hyperscaler Q3 reports expected around Oct 28-29, estimates not confirmed; FOMC Oct 27-28). EDGAR checked 10/2 shows no new 8-K since the 9/22 convert closing, only more Form 4/144 insider-sale filings. The lower 12-month fair value does not change a one-month view (valuation barely moves a stock in a month), so the 1-month ladder is unchanged. Round 3: the GPU-life rebuild changes a long-run cash-flow view, not anything inside the October window, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged again. Round 4: the site inventory and split discount rate change the long-run cash-flow view only. The one event in the window that touches a site (Applied Digital's last 75 MW at Polaris Forge 1 going live on 10/2) is already scheduled and contracted, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged.

fair_value.method: Equal-weight blend of a site-level GPU-cohort DCF ($0: every regime/k cell is negative equity even with signed-contract cash at 8.75%; unfloored -$39.6 split / -$43.8 single at Oct-27) and an EV/EBITDA exit (~$92: 6.0x Oct-2027 NTM adj. EBITDA $19.7B less ~$61B net debt plus $0.3B JV net, over 622M shares). Blend = $46, below the $88.57 spot.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Rebuilt bottom-up as a site-level GPU-cohort DCF: every inventory site appears once with its MW, landlord lease (CoreWeave pays: Core Scientific $1.44M, Applied Digital $1.8M, Galaxy $1.9M, Blockfusion $2.2M per MW-yr; $1.8-2.0M where undisclosed), energisation date and contract status. Per MW: contract revenue $10.3M/yr (exit-2026 ARR $19B / 1.85 GW), capex k x revenue (k 2.5/2.7x), 59.5% adj. EBITDA at contract price after rent, power/site ops $0.65M per MW-yr, so fixed cost is ~24-27% of contract revenue (was 18%); SBC 4%; contract term mix 4/5/6 yrs, then the round-3 rental path (normal 60% / shortage 40%); 6-yr life, refresh at 0.85k, 9% salvage; per-MW revenue, leases and power escalate 2%/yr; cash tax 21% from 2030. Buckets: energized 1,700 MW (capex sunk, signed contracts) +$33.3B; contracted power not yet energized 2,343 MW (leased: 95% delivery, 50% already customer-signed per RPO math, 85% of the rest sign, else the shell is stranded at 50% sublet for 15 yrs; owned Kenilworth/Hammond at 0.9/0.6 completion x 0.85 customer, net of shell capex) -$10.2B; uncontracted pipeline (1,200 MW powered land at p 0.5 from 2030; 2,300 MW NVIDIA-framework gap to 8 GW at p 0.25 from 2031) -$6.2B; JV equity net of remaining funding +$0.29B; exited Poolside and the Core Scientific merger at 0. Split discounting: cash inside signed contract terms (and the capex committed to deliver them) at 8.75%; post-contract, unsigned, pipeline and terminal cash at the 11.5% WACC. Probability-weighted EV $16.7B split ($14.6B single), less $37B net debt, over 576M shares (unvested RSUs removed because future SBC is deducted). Per share today, split rate: normal k2.5 -$30.4, k2.7 -$55.9; shortage k2.5 -$9.5, k2.7 -$35.0. Every cell is negative, so the floored value is $0 both ways; unfloored weighted -$34.8 today / -$39.6 Oct-27 (single rate -$38.4 / -$43.8). Sensitivities (Oct-27, unfloored, split): life 5y -$81.5, 7y -$32.9, 8y -$35.9; no salvage -$65; WACC 11% -$34.5; contracted rate 5.9% (DDTL 4.0 coupon) -$34.2; no pipeline -$27.3; margin 62% -$20.2 (floored $1.8); k 2.3x +$3.9 (floored $7.3, single $5.6); no per-MW growth or escalation -$24.7.

inputs_detail.derivation: Midpoint of raised FY26 guidance $12.4-13.2B.

inputs_detail.value: $24.2B (site-built: energized MW plus each site's delivery date)
inputs_detail.derivation: Sum of site revenue: 1.7 GW energized at 10/1/26 plus 2027 deliveries at their latest dates (Helios II H1-27 after a ~1-yr slip, Dalton P2 early 2027, PF1 third building mid-2027, Cheyenne end-2026, Lancaster mid-2027, Bell SK H1-27). ~8% below the $26.3B consensus because of the delivery slips (Helios II, DDTL 3.0 covenant reset 'to align with delivery schedule', Poolside exit).

No longer a top-down path sized to 8 GW. 4.2 GW contracted power is delivered site by site (Indonesia ~2028, Helios III 2028); the uncontracted 1.2 GW powered land/options/LOIs comes in at 50% from 2030 and the 2.3 GW gap to the 8 GW target at 25% from 2031 (the NVIDIA 5 GW framework overlaps, so it is not added). Revenue then follows each cohort's contract/re-lease path; per-MW revenue rises 2%/yr. Fixes flags F1, F6 (one MW conversion, $10.3M per MW-yr) and F7.

inputs_detail.value: 59.5% at contract price after data-center rent; fixed cost (lease $1.44-2.2M + power/site ops $0.65M per MW-yr) = ~24-27% of contract revenue, variable ~14-16%
inputs_detail.derivation: Reported 56-62% over five quarters (59% in Q2'26). Round 3 used 18% fixed; flag F3 shows observed CoreWeave leases of $1.44M (Core Scientific), $1.8M (Applied Digital), $1.9M (Galaxy), $2.2M (Blockfusion LOI) per MW-yr before power, i.e. 20-27% of $10.3M revenue per MW. Fixed cost is now each site's own lease plus $0.65M power/ops, which shortens the post-contract cash tail. The margin at contract price is unchanged; only the fixed/variable split moved.

inputs_detail.input: SBC as % of revenue (treated as cash cost)
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2'26 SBC $165M on $2,575M revenue = 6.4%; declines with scale.

inputs_detail.input: Capex intensity k (capex per $ of incremental annual revenue)
inputs_detail.value: 2.5x and 2.7x, equally weighted (central ~2.6x = ~$27M per MW at $10.3M revenue per MW-yr); refresh 0.85k; owned shells add $5.5M/MW (Kenilworth remaining) or $8M/MW (Hammond, owned pipeline)
inputs_detail.derivation: 10-Q: in-service gross PP&E ~$40.7B vs Q2 annualized revenue $10.3B = ~3.95x on a ramping base (corrected from round 3's 3.5x, as the supervisor noted). 2026 capex guide midpoint $37B over the ~$13.5B 2027 revenue increment = 2.7x. Equal weight on 2.5x and 2.7x as in round 3. Capex for sites energizing after 10/1/26 is now charged from Q4-26 (round 3 charged it by revenue path). Owned shells: Kenilworth $1.8B project less ~$0.7B spent (purchase $322M plus a year of construction), over ~200 MW IT.
Midpoint of raised FY26 capex guidance $35-39B.

inputs_detail.value: Contract price for 4y (35%) / 5y (35%) / 6y (30%) of each cohort; 3% of revenue uncontracted at spot
inputs_detail.derivation: FY25 10-K: committed contracts were over 98% of 2025 revenue (96% in 2024), with a weighted-average contract duration of about five years at 12/31/25 (about four at 12/31/24). The 10-Q RPO profile (41% in 24 months, 39% in 25-48, 20% beyond) fits a ~5-yr average with a tail beyond 4 yrs. The DDTL 5.5's ~3-yr average contracts are one facility, so I do not use them for the whole fleet.

inputs_detail.input: Post-contract rental path (market price vs original contract price, by cohort age)
inputs_detail.value: Normal regime (60%): 1.50/1.05/0.80/0.74/0.68/0.58/0.47/0.30 for ages 1-8; shortage regime (40%): x1.4, capped at 1.0
inputs_detail.derivation: The contract price is set at about the market price around age 2. The H100 index fell ~50% in ~18 months after its successor shipped, then held near $2.80: 1.50 -> 0.80 over ages 1-3, then ~0.7 at ages 3-5. A100 at age ~6 rents at 23-39% of launch (Silicon Data $1.58, Ornn $0.93): 0.58/1.50 = 39%. Ornn prices A100/H100/B200 at about the same cost per PFLOP-hr, so old chips reprice with the cost of compute rather than to scrap. Resale falls faster than rent (CCIR), hence the steeper drop at ages 7-8. The shortage regime matches CoreWeave's re-booking of an expiring H100 cluster at ~95% of the original price and the A100 contract into 2029; it gets 40% because those data come from a supply- and power-constrained market, while most of this model's value comes from 2027-30 cohorts re-contracting in 2032-36.

inputs_detail.value: 6 years base (cohort retired and refreshed at end of age 6); 5, 7 and 8 years shown; refresh capex 0.85k; salvage 9% at 6y (12% at 5y, 6% at 7y, 4% at 8y); book D&A 6 years
inputs_detail.derivation: Kept from round 3. Fact-checked company lives: CoreWeave 6 (10-K), Nebius 5 (from Jan 2026), IREN 5 (HPC hardware; round 3 wrongly said 6), hyperscalers 5-6 (MSFT/GOOGL/ORCL 6, META 5.5, AMZN cut a subset 6->5). CoreWeave discloses no salvage value; it does not state zero (round 3's 'no salvage' wording corrected). In the site model value peaks at 7 yrs (-$32.9 vs -$39.6 at 6), which is not enough to change the base. Salvage from CCIR executed resale prices times a ~60% GPU share of capex, less removal costs.
Rf 5.29% (10y UST 9/30/26) + adjusted beta 1.94 (raw weekly beta 2.40 vs QQQ over 52 weeks, Blume-adjusted) x ERP 4.5% (Damodaran implied 4.14% Sept 2026, rounded up for high-beta regime).

inputs_detail.value: 9.0% pre-tax; ~8.1% after a partial tax shield
inputs_detail.derivation: Q3'26 interest guide $860-940M a quarter on ~$40B of debt = ~9% annualized; management says the weighted average cost of debt fell almost 300bp in the past year (~$1.1B annual saving on the end-Q2 debt load); marginal unsecured notes 9-9.75% and SOFR+5.5% DDTL 5.5, offset by 2.875% converts. Round 1 used 8.5% with a full 21% shield; the supervisor flagged that a full shield is inconsistent with ~zero cash taxes while NOLs/losses last, so I apply about half the shield.

~59% equity ($53.6B = 605M x $88.57) / 41% net debt (~$37B): 0.59x14.0% + 0.41x8.1% = 11.6% -> 11.5%. With no shield it is ~11.9%, with a full shield ~11.2%; round 1's 11.0% is shown as a sensitivity as the supervisor asked.

6/30/26 debt principal $35.6B less $6.9B liquidity, plus Q3 burn and the $566M capped call, less convert proceeds in cash = ~$37B at 9/30/26 (converts as debt). Flag F5: JV commitments now in the bridge. Remaining funding (two JVs: $1.7B committed less $479M carrying; NJ JV $160M max less $44M) of $1.34B is a liability; JV equity is valued at 0.9x total commitment ($1.67B); 50% of the $95M guarantee is deducted: net +$0.29B. Operating leases stay out of net debt because rent is charged in the site cash flows.

inputs_detail.value: 576M (DCF); 622M at Oct-27 for the EV/EBITDA leg
inputs_detail.derivation: 551.5M Class A+B at 7/31/26 plus 24M options (avg strike $1.84) = 576M. Unvested RSUs (29M) are dropped from the DCF count because future SBC is deducted as a cash cost (the supervisor flagged a ~$2-3/share double count). The EV/EBITDA leg uses adj. EBITDA before SBC, so it keeps RSUs (605M + ~17M ATM = 622M).

US statutory 21% on positive EBIT after ~$4B of NOL use (accumulated deficit $4.0B with valuation allowance); model EBIT stays small until ~2029-30, so cash taxes are near zero before then, which is why the Kd shield is only partial.

With no dividends, today's DCF equity value is grown at the 14% cost of equity. Every cell is negative, so the floored value is $0 today and in Oct-27; unfloored weighted -$34.8 today -> -$39.6 Oct-27 (split rate).

inputs_detail.input: Scenario weights over rental regime and k
inputs_detail.value: regime normal 60% / shortage 40%; k 2.5x / 2.7x 50/50; 6-yr life; cells floored at $0 (unfloored also shown)
inputs_detail.derivation: Unchanged from round 3. Floors are kept for comparability. Now every cell is negative (best: shortage k2.5 -$9.5 today), so the floored DCF is $0 and the equity's option value on a 93%-vol, long-dated-debt company is not in this number. A Merton-style check (EV ~$22B, ~$45B debt face, 5 yrs, 40% asset vol) puts it at ~$4-8 a share; I note it but do not add it.

inputs_detail.input: Discount rate on signed-contract cash flows
inputs_detail.value: 8.75% blended (IG 7.5%, Jane Street 8.5%, OpenAI/Anthropic 9.5%, other unnamed 10.0%, short-dated Q3 contracts 10.75%); 11.5% WACC for everything else; stranded-lease payments at the 9% cost of debt
inputs_detail.derivation: Anchor: DDTL 4.0 (Meta Aa3/AA- order, A3 non-recourse) priced at 2.00% + the 3.14-yr Treasury = ~5.9% in Mar-2026. The 3-yr UST has risen from ~3.85% to 4.91% (10/1/26), so the same structure costs ~6.9% today; add ~60bp for completion/operating risk and the 0-10% equity slice -> 7.5% for Meta/NVIDIA/Microsoft cash. Jane Street (Fitch BBB-, Moody's Ba1) 8.5%. OpenAI-backed DDTL 3.0 at SOFR+400 (~8.1%, ~8.9% fixed-equivalent) -> 9.5%, also used for unrated Anthropic. Unnamed contracts behind DDTL 5.0 (S+450, parent guarantee) 10.0%. Short-dated contracts behind DDTL 5.5 (S+550) 10.75%. Weights by value x duration (IG ~37% of ~$125B book and the longest, to 2032): 0.49/0.05/0.19/0.16/0.11 -> 8.66%, rounded to 8.75%. Per-site counterparties are not disclosed, so one blended rate is applied to all signed-contract cash. Committed lease payments of stranded shells are a CoreWeave obligation, so they are discounted at its ~9% cost of debt, not at the contract rate.

inputs_detail.input: Contracted vs uncontracted MW and probabilities
inputs_detail.value: Energized 1,700 MW (named 990 + 710 MW pool at undisclosed-MW sites); contracted to come 2,500 MW (named 1,853 + 647 MW unattributed); pipeline 1,200 MW at p 0.5 and 2,300 MW at p 0.25
inputs_detail.derivation: Active 1.5 GW at 6/30 and >1.85 GW at YE26 -> ~1.7 GW at 10/1. Contracted 4.2 GW (8/11) less 1.7 = 2.5 GW to come; RPO $103.7B + >$25B Q3 commitments covers ~1.7 GW energized x ~3.5 yrs and ~1.1 GW of new capacity x ~5 yrs at $10.3M, so ~50% of the leased to-come MW is customer-signed. The pipeline probabilities are judgment: the company itself counts the 1.5 GW (gross; ~1.2 GW IT) toward 8 GW, but Poolside's 250 MW (+500 MW reserved) was cancelled within six months and Helios II slipped a year; the NVIDIA framework is 'subject to future agreements'.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 6.0x NTM adj. EBITDA at Oct 2027 ($19.7B) = EV $118B; less net debt ~$61B; plus JV net +$0.3B; = equity ~$57B / 622M shares = ~$92 (unchanged).

inputs_detail.derivation: EV ~$90.6B ($53.6B equity + ~$37B net debt) / NTM EBITDA ~$14.1B (Q4'26 implied revenue $4.6B from guidance + Q1-Q3'27 ~$18.8B on the consensus path, at 60% margin).

CRWV's own current ~6.4x, trimmed slightly because growth slows from ~100% to ~45%. Not a peer multiple: Nebius has negative EBITDA and is not comparable. Round 3: kept. The research says value is front-loaded, which argues that EBITDA overstates sustainable cash, but the multiple is the market's own price for CRWV and already reflects the public life debate (Kerrisdale, Burry), so I do not cut it a second time.

~$34B NTM revenue (exit-2027 run-rate >$30B per mgmt, rising into 2028) x 58% margin. Round 4 cross-check: the site-built path (2027 $24.2B, 2028 $38.0B) interpolates to ~$34.5B for Q4'27-Q3'28, so NTM EBITDA is kept despite the lower 2027.

$37B at 9/30/26 (6/30 principal $35.6B less $6.9B liquidity, plus Q3 burn and the $566M capped call; the $4.137B convert proceeds are netted) + Q4'26 FCFF burn ~$7.5B + 9 months of 2027 burn ~$11.8B (DCF path with 2027 revenue $26.3B) + ~$5.0B cash interest over five quarters (Q3'26 guide $0.86-0.94B, rising with the debt) - ~$1.5B ATM proceeds = ~$59.8B. Measured at 2027-10-01, not year-end. The supervisor reconciles ~$61B; each $5B is ~$8 a share. Round 3: the cohort model needs ~$1B more 2027 capex (9 months) to replace revenue from early cohorts re-pricing in 2028, so ~$61B, which also matches the supervisor's reconciled figure.
605M diluted plus ~17M issued from the 35M-share ATM program.

bear.story: AI-capex digestion or a Customer A wobble (36% of Q2, 40% of H1 revenue, unnamed) meets ~$61B of Oct-2027 net debt. Blackwell/Rubin supply and new power ease the shortage, so Hopper re-contract pricing falls toward the normal-regime path (~0.7 of the original contract at ages 4-5) and the market starts pricing the front-loaded GPU economics in the cohort DCF. EV/EBITDA compresses to ~4.5x on ~$17B EBITDA and leverage roughly halves the equity. Round 4: site-level risks add a path: unsigned contracted-power sites (~1.2 GW leased with no customer yet, plus Indonesia's 360 MW) fail to sign, leaving CoreWeave paying 12-15-yr leases on empty shells.

base.story: Execution on guidance, but the 2027 ramp runs a little behind consensus: the site-by-site schedule (Helios II H1-27 after a ~1-yr slip, Dalton P2, PF1 third building, Lancaster mid-2027, Indonesia ~2028) gives ~$24B of 2027 revenue vs $26.3B consensus, while the exit-2027 run-rate still nears $30B. Rentals stay firm through the window, so the market keeps valuing CRWV on ~6x NTM EBITDA, not on a cash-flow model near zero, and the stock drifts below today's price as net debt climbs.

bull.story: The shortage persists: expiring Hopper clusters re-book at ~95% of the original price, A100s keep earning into 2029 and the ~25% July increase sticks, which supports a 7+ year life (the shortage-regime cells, ~$23 today at k 2.5x, rising quickly with lower k). Margins move toward the long-term target and financing costs fall. The multiple re-rates to ~8x on ~$21B forward EBITDA. Round 4: even then, the site DCF needs k <=2.3x or the 62% margin to show positive equity, so the bull case rests on the multiple.

thesis_break_reason: Kept at ~$55 (supervisor's reconciled level $48). A sustained close below ~$55, under the July-2026 low of $60.55 and ~38% below today, would most likely mean a fundamental problem rather than 93%-vol noise: a Customer A cut or delay, a failed or punitive financing, a guidance cut on delivery delays, or evidence that re-contract pricing for Hopper/Ampere is falling toward the normal-regime path (~0.7 of the original contract at re-contract). That last case is where the round-3 cohort DCF is clearly negative equity in every cell. At $55, equity is ~$34B against ~$45B of net debt by early 2027 and ~$61B by Oct-2027. I keep $55 rather than $48 because the GPU-life rebuild leaves even less cash-flow cushion than round 2 did. Round 4: kept at $55. The site model adds one specific break signal: a contracted-power site losing its delivery date or its customer (as Poolside did), because the 12-15-yr leases leave CoreWeave paying for empty shells.

key_uncertainties: Post-contract GPU rental path, capex intensity and economic life. In the site model every regime/k cell is negative equity at a 6-yr life, even with signed-contract cash at 8.75%; only k <=2.3x (+$4 unfloored, +$7 floored) or a ~62% margin in the shortage regime shows positive equity. Energized sites are worth ~$19M per MW (+$33B); new contracted builds and pipeline are value-destroying at k 2.6 (-$16B). This is the gap between the $0 DCF and the ~$92 multiple value.

Site execution and customer signing: ~1.2 GW of leased contracted power and Indonesia's 360 MW have no disclosed customer, while CoreWeave owes 12-15-yr rent on them (Core Scientific 590 MW, Galaxy 526 MW, Applied Digital 400 MW = ~36% of contracted power across three landlords). Helios II has slipped ~1 yr, Poolside was cancelled, and the DDTL 3.0 covenants were reset to the delivery schedule.
Customer concentration: Customer A 36% of Q2 / 40% of H1-26 revenue and Customer B 26% / 23% (unnamed in the 10-Q); top 3 were 72% of Q2
Financing access and cost: ~$35.6B of debt principal at mid-2026 rising to ~$60B net debt by Oct-2027 at ~9% marginal cost; each $5B of net debt is ~$8 a share
Dilution: 35M-share ATM, $4.2B 2033 converts (conversion price $97.85, capped-call cap $199.70), 2031/2032 converts ($107.80/$119.60), evergreen equity plans
Execution on power and data-center delivery (third-party delays in Nov 2025; local opposition to data centers)
Durability of AI-capex demand and the competitive response from hyperscalers and other neoclouds
Internal-control material weaknesses still being remediated ahead of the first 404 attestation
reasoning: Round 4 (site coverage and split discount rate). I replaced the top-down revenue path with a site-level build. Each of the 45 inventory sites appears once. Energized sites (1.7 GW: 990 MW named plus a 710 MW pool split across sites with undisclosed MW) carry sunk capex and signed contracts. Contracted sites not yet energized (2.5 GW) carry their own delivery date and their own lease, which CoreWeave pays the landlord. About half of them are customer-signed per RPO math; the rest sign with 85% probability or are stranded at 50% sublet. The owned self-builds (Kenilworth, Hammond) are probability-weighted net of shell capex, and so is the uncontracted pipeline (1.2 GW at 50%, the 2.3 GW gap to 8 GW at 25%, no double count with the NVIDIA framework). The JV commitments enter the net-debt bridge; Poolside and the Core Scientific merger are removed. The supervisor's corrections are applied: fixed cost 18% -> ~25% from the actual leases (F3), in-service PP&E/revenue 3.95x, and unvested RSUs out of the DCF share count. Signed-contract cash is discounted at 8.75%, a blend anchored on DDTL 4.0 (Meta-backed, ~5.9% at pricing, ~6.9% at today's Treasuries) and the S+400 to S+550 facilities. Everything else stays at the 11.5% WACC. The split adds ~$2.1B of EV, ~$4 a share: modest, because the contract years are short (~5 yrs) and the value problem sits in the post-contract tail and the refresh/new-build capex at k 2.6. Result: energized sites are worth ~$33B, new contracted builds -$10B, pipeline -$6B, so EV is $16.7B (split) / $14.6B (single) against $37B net debt. Every cell is negative, so the floored DCF is $0 both ways (round 3 $2). Unfloored at Oct-27 it is -$39.6 split / -$43.8 single, against round 3's -$26. The difference comes from the higher lease-based fixed cost, Q4-26 capex for 2027 sites, stranded-lease risk, per-MW escalation, and the smaller share count. The EV/EBITDA leg stays at $92: the site path interpolates to the same ~$34B NTM revenue at Oct-27 even though 2027 itself falls to ~$24B. Fair value $47 -> $46. As in rounds 2-3 I move the 12-month ladder only a little, because CRWV trades on the multiple and AI-capex sentiment and nothing in the window tests the long-run cash flows: median ~$73 -> ~$71.5 for the 2027 delivery-slip evidence; base $80 -> $78, bull $155 -> $150; thesis break $55 kept. The 1-month ladder is unchanged. Research this round: the site inventory and contracts_credit table, one WebFetch of CoreWeave's Q3 contracting release (confirming >$25B on ~3-6 month contracts at ~$40M/MW), the Treasury yield curve, and the GPU-life fact-check. No web searches.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Contract price for the contract term (35% 4y / 35% 5y / 30% 6y; >98% committed), then the market path vs the original contract price by age 1-8: normal regime (60%) 1.50/1.05/0.80/0.74/0.68/0.58/0.47/0.30 (steep for ~2 yrs after the next generation, flat ~0.7 at ages 3-5, then down); shortage regime (40%) x1.4 capped at 1.0. Blended cohort revenue vs year 1: normal 1.00/0.99/0.98/0.98/0.87/0.69/0.46/0.30; shortage 1.00/0.99/0.99/0.99/0.97/0.85/0.65/0.41. Fixed cash cost is now each site's lease ($1.44-2.2M per MW-yr) plus $0.65M power/ops (~24-27% of contract revenue, escalating 2%/yr), so the cash tail ends sooner (price below ~30% of contract). Refresh at the end of the life at 0.85k, with 9% salvage (12% at 5y, 6% at 7y).
gpu_life.note: Per share at Oct-27, probability-weighted over regime (60/40) and k 2.5/2.7x, cells floored at $0, split-rate site DCF. Every cell is negative at 5, 6 and 7 yrs, so all floored values are $0. Unfloored (split / single): 5y -$81.5 / -$85.1; 6y -$39.6 / -$43.8; 7y -$32.9 / -$37.0; 8y -$35.9 / -$40.0 (value peaks near 7 yrs). Round 3 floored 0/2/5.3, unfloored central -$26. Lives fact-checked: CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5, IREN 5. CoreWeave owns and rents the GPUs, so the research applies in full. Most sensitive inputs: k (2.3x lifts the 6-yr value to +$3.9 unfloored / $7.3 floored), salvage (none: -$65) and margin (62%: -$20).

discounting.basis: Signed-contract cash flows, and the capex committed to deliver them, are discounted at 8.75%: a value-and-duration-weighted blend of IG (Meta Aa3, NVIDIA Aa1, Microsoft Aaa) 7.5%, Jane Street (BBB-/Ba1) 8.5%, OpenAI/Anthropic (unrated) 9.5%, other unnamed (DDTL 5.0, S+450) 10.0% and short-dated Q3 contracts (DDTL 5.5, S+550) 10.75%. The IG rate is anchored on DDTL 4.0, a non-recourse A3 facility against the Meta contract at 2.00% + 3.14-yr UST (~5.9% at Mar-26 pricing, ~6.9% at the 4.91% 3-yr UST on 10/1/26), plus ~60bp for completion/operating risk and the equity slice. Post-contract, unsigned, pipeline and terminal cash flows stay at the 11.5% WACC; stranded-lease obligations are discounted at the 9% cost of debt. dcf_single_rate and dcf_split_rate are the floored per-share values at Oct-27 used in fair value (both $0 because every cell is negative). Unfloored: single -$43.8, split -$39.6 (today -$38.4 / -$34.8). EV $14.6B single vs $16.7B split. Floored at k 2.3x: $5.6 single vs $7.3 split. site_coverage value_per_share is each site's probability-weighted split-rate EV contribution per share today (576M shares, before net debt). The rows sum to $29.45; less $64.24 net debt per share that gives the -$34.8 unfloored equity today.
